facts.t: Both Commissions landed on the same number
facts.d: 41% vertical devolution twice in a row. The 16th Finance Commission's continuity gives the figure what its own report calls a semi-permanence — the first time a devolution share has effectively stabilised across award periods.

facts.t: The grand bargain is a trade, not a gift
facts.d: The 16th Commission floated the idea that states accept a smaller percentage share in exchange for a materially larger divisible pool, if the Centre merges cesses and surcharges into shareable taxes. A smaller slice of a bigger pie.

facts.t: Tax effort was dropped after decades in the formula
facts.d: Rewarding states for collecting their own revenue had been a fixture of devolution formulas. The 16th Commission removed it and added contribution to GDP instead — shifting the efficiency incentive from collection to production.

bank.q: The 16th Finance Commission is chaired by:
bank.e: Arvind Panagariya. N. K. Singh chaired the 15th Finance Commission.

bank.q: Comparing the two Commissions, consider the following statements:
s: The 16th Finance Commission's award period runs from 2026-27 to 2030-31.
Both derive their mandate from Article 280.
bank.e: All three are correct. The 15th covered 2021-22 to 2025-26 with an additional year for 2020-21.

bank.q: Match List I (criterion) with List II (16th FC weight):
bank.e: Income distance 42.5%, population 17.5%, area 10% and the new contribution-to-GDP criterion 10%. Demographic performance is 10% and forest and ecology 10%.

bank.q: Which one of the following criteria was NOT carried forward by the 16th Finance Commission?
bank.e: Tax and fiscal effort, which carried 2.5% under the 15th Commission, was dropped altogether.

bank.q: With reference to changes made by the 16th Finance Commission, consider the following:
s: Sector-specific and state-specific grants are replaced by rule-based, performance-linked instruments.
The weight on income distance was increased.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Income distance fell from 45% to 42.5% — a slight dilution of pure equity.

bank.as: The 16th Finance Commission adds a contribution-to-GDP criterion.
bank.rs: It seeks to rebalance the formula between equity and efficiency.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. Equity is retained through income distance while efficiency enters through a growth-oriented parameter.

bank.q: The divisible pool is calculated as gross central taxes minus:
bank.e: All three deductions apply, which is why rising cesses shrink the effective share reaching states even when the headline percentage is unchanged.

bank.q: All of the following describe the direction of change from the 15th to the 16th Commission EXCEPT:
o: A stronger, more emphatic population-control incentive
bank.e: Demographic performance fell from 12.5% to 10% — the incentive continues but is less emphatic.

bank.q: Which pair of criteria carries identical weight under both Commissions?
bank.e: Forest and ecology stays at 10% in both — the only criterion unchanged across the two formulas.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the grand bargain proposal:
s: States would accept a smaller percentage share of the divisible pool.
In return the Centre would merge cesses and surcharges into shareable taxes.
It has already been implemented through a constitutional amendment.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 describe the proposal. It remains a proposal — no amendment has given it effect.
